publications.name: Infrequent Trading, Asymmetrical Asset Price Volatility, and Welfare Loss (JMP)
publications.summary: As more assets face infrequent trading restrictions or horizon-bound illiquidity through real estate holdings, private equity lockups, household infrequent adjustment, and institutional vesting requirements, we develop a finite-horizon, continuous-time heterogeneous-agent model to analyze how explicit trading restrictions affect risk sharing and asset prices. Modeling a restricted investor and a liquid market maker, we identify an endogenous liquidity squeeze. The restricted agent optimally holds excess equity at time zero to self-insure against an inability to rebalance, starving the market maker of capital and forcing suboptimal positions. This friction generates excess price volatility and jump risks, including block trades and yield curve jumps when liquidity is restored. Welfare losses depend asymmetrically on the capitalization of liquid agents rather than the duration of restrictions. The endogenous price distortions created by illiquidity can produce aggregate welfare losses that outweigh the classic costs of fundamental business cycles.

publications.name: Optimal Renovation and Lease Renewal in a Principal-Agent Framework
Rogue Agent: The Economics of Compute in the Agentic Age
publications.summary: This paper develops a task-based model in which heterogeneous software tasks are allocated across human, reasoning-assisted, and agentic workflows. When agentic compute costs grow faster than labor savings, agentic coding is eventually excluded for sufficiently complex tasks. Under additional restrictions, optimal agentic usage is concentrated in an intermediate or low-complexity region. Initial compute capacity shifts tasks from unaided human production to reasoning-assisted workflows, while additional capacity expands agentic coding. Even when compute constraints cease to bind, reasoning remains optimal for a subset of tasks. The results highlight task composition and internal compute governance as central determinants of organizational AI adoption.

publications.name: Price to Rent Ratio
publications.summary: The decision to rent or purchase a home is influenced by volatile and heterogeneous price-to-rent ratios. This study introduces a leveraged variance decomposition model to investigate how mortgage leverage affects local price-to-rent ratios. Individual property-level rents are estimated using a neural network calibrated with Census microdata, Dewey RentHub data, and CoreLogic property characteristics. The methodology examines ZIP-code-level relationships between price-to-rent ratios and leverage using a modified Campbell-Shiller decomposition. The analysis aims to establish the effect of leverage on price-to-rent volatility and the role of expected future real interest rates.
